claims.text: Reject alias lists containing empty parts (e.g., "a||b", "|", "a|") at compile time to prevent named arguments called ""
claims.quote: Alias lists with empty parts still compile, such as "a||b", "|" and "a|". At runtime the empty part becomes a named argument called "". Rejecting it may be worth it while you are here.
claims.status_note: author declined, explaining empty strings carry no risk and don't need compile-time linting
claims.status_by_quote: I'd say that is fine, because there is no risk.
